citation: Elpidorou, A., & Freeman, L. (2015). Affectivity in Heidegger I: Moods and Emotions in Being and Time. Philosophy Compass, 10(10), 661–671. https://doi.org/10.1111/phc3.12236
thesis: Reconstructs Heidegger's Being and Time account of mood (Befindlichkeit/Stimmung) as constitutive, pre-reflective, world-disclosing, and prior to any subject/object or consciousness model, using anxiety as the paradigm case; closes by proposing that moods are the necessary background condition for occurrent, intentionally-directed emotions. Explicitly the first half of a two-part study; boredom and BT's temporal structure are reserved for the companion essay (bor-sec-03).

sections.title: Introduction — affective experience as ubiquitous, meaningful, revelatory; moods as constitutive of Dasein
The Project of Fundamental Ontology in Being and Time — Dasein, disclosedness (Erschlossenheit), the four existentials, care (Sorge)
Befindlichkeit and affective disclosedness — untranslatability; Befindlichkeit/Stimmung as ontological/ontic; moods as atmospheres, pre-reflective and unthematic
Befindlichkeit's three essential characteristics — mood discloses thrownness, being-in-the-world as a whole, and what matters
Thrownness, anxiety, and fallenness — evasive turning-away; anxiety as the exceptional turning-toward; anxiety as Grundbefindlichkeit grounding fear
Conclusion: The Place of Emotions in Being and Time — Heidegger's silence on emotion; fear's ambiguous status; moods as background for emotions
Endnotes 1-15, incl. translation-history survey (n.4) and explicit deferral of Befindlichkeit's temporal structure/boredom to the companion essay (n.13)

readings.text: Befindlichkeit (ontological) and Stimmung (ontic) name one and the same phenomenon under two aspects; Dasein is always in some mood, even indifference counts as a mood.

Moods are not inner subjective states inferred from behavior; they are pre-given 'atmospheres' in which Dasein exists, disclosive in a pre-reflective, unthematic way, and more primordially revealing than theoretical/cognitive disclosure.

Mood discloses three things equiprimordially: thrownness (Geworfenheit), being-in-the-world as a whole (with Mitdasein and one's own existence), and what matters (mattering is grounded in Befindlichkeit).
Thrownness is for the most part disclosed only via an evasive turning-away: Dasein flees into worldly busyness and 'the they' rather than confronting its own facticity.

Anxiety is the exceptional turning-away that is not a fleeing: it springs from Dasein itself, strips the everyday world of significance without making it absent, and throws Dasein back on its own potentiality-for-Being.

Anxiety is Grundbefindlichkeit, the ground-attunement that makes other moods (including fear) possible; fear is an inauthentic mode of Befindlichkeit because its turning-away is a genuine fleeing from oneself, unlike anxiety's.

Fear's classification is unstable: directed at a determinate worldly entity, it looks more like an occurrent emotion than a mood — a tension flagged (via Freeman 2015 and Blattner 2006) rather than resolved.
Heidegger's near-silence on emotion in BT follows from the text's ontological (not ontic) aim, but an account of affectivity without emotion is judged incomplete.

Authors' own proposal: moods are the necessary background against which occurrent, intentionally-specific emotions arise, because emotions require a mattering world and mattering is grounded only in mood; this also resolves the fear puzzle via Heidegger's own 'fearfulness' (Furchtsamkeit).

interlocutors.name: Martin Heidegger
interlocutors.role: primary text under analysis (Being and Time; also Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics, History of the Concept of Time/Prolegomena, Zollikon Seminars)

interlocutors.name: Andreas Elpidorou (self-cite)
interlocutors.role: authors cite their own 2013 'Moods and Appraisals' in support of the moods-ground-emotions proposal; also a cluster-hub author (bor-sec-03 through -06, -25, -26)

interlocutors.name: Lauren Freeman (self-cite)
interlocutors.role: co-author's own 2014/2015 pieces cited on the mood/emotion relationship and the fear-as-emotion reading

interlocutors.name: William Blattner
interlocutors.role: cited for the 'affectedness'/'affectivity' translation of Befindlichkeit and for agreeing fear may not be a mode of Befindlichkeit

interlocutors.name: Matthew Ratcliffe
interlocutors.role: cited (2008, 2013) in support of moods as background for intentionally-directed states, and on anxiety's relation to fear

interlocutors.name: Jan Slaby
interlocutors.role: cited (2014) in support of the moods-as-background-for-emotions proposal

interlocutors.name: Charles Guignon
interlocutors.role: cited for the 'situatedness' translation of Befindlichkeit and the 'mood' (not 'attunement') rendering of Stimmung

interlocutors.name: Hubert Dreyfus
interlocutors.role: cited for the 'affectedness' translation and for 'mood' over 'attunement' for Stimmung

interlocutors.name: Taylor Carman
interlocutors.role: cited among translators using 'disposition'/'disposedness' for Befindlichkeit

interlocutors.name: Daniel Dahlstrom
interlocutors.role: cited among translators using 'disposition' and for further discussion of the translation problem

interlocutors.name: John Haugeland
interlocutors.role: cited for the 'findingness' neologism and objections to 'disposition' as importing subjectivity

interlocutors.name: Macquarrie & Robinson
interlocutors.role: BT's English translators; their 'state-of-mind' rendering of Befindlichkeit is judged problematic

tensions.label: Befindlichkeit translation debate
tensions.poles: 'state-of-mind' (Macquarrie & Robinson) vs. 'disposition/disposedness' (Carman, Dahlstrom, Kisiel, Wrathall) vs. 'ontological disposition' (Mayr & Askay) vs. 'findingness' (Haugeland) vs. 'affectedness/affectivity' (Dreyfus, Blattner, Crowell) vs. 'situatedness' (Guignon) vs. 'attunement' (Stambaugh) vs. left untranslated (this essay's own choice)

tensions.label: Is fear a mood or an emotion?
tensions.poles: fear as Befindlichkeit/mood (textual placement in BT §30) vs. fear as occurrent, object-directed emotion (Freeman 2015, Blattner 2006, and the authors' own leaning)

tensions.label: Anxiety vs. profound boredom as candidate Grundstimmung
tensions.poles: BT's anxiety as the (nearly unique, BT 358/310) ground-attunement vs. FCM's later naming of profound boredom as the Grundstimmung of contemporary Dasein (a post-1929 development this essay flags but does not pursue)
